A timeout that long sounds like a dhcp issue. Things I can think of:

  • your dhcp lease drops after 36h and does not get released/renewed properly - check on your router for the dhcp timeout

  • there is something wrong with your dns settings; check for errors in the dns section of the network applet, or on your router if you get them through dhcp.

  • check if the trouble persists if you disable the firewall when the connection bugs out: sudo ufw disable (and sudo ufw enable to switch on again)
Yeah, but if there were a dns/dhcp problem, would it not affect all connections?

Yep, unless some ip/hostname configurations are in your hosts file. If they are, you don't need dns to resolve the ip for those hostnames and they will work. Others that aren't in your hosts file won't work. Can't think of anything else that has a 36h timeout.

This is just a SWAG, given that I haven't seen any logs, but I think @thepower hit on something important for your troubleshooting purposes. Ubuntu, and by inheritance Mint, use NetworkManager configured to point to the local dnsmasq resolver for lookups. This can be quirky, at best, in some situations. The first thing I would do if I were you is disable dnsmasq as your resolver, allowing your lookups to function in a traditional way; this is easily reversible, and it's going to make troubleshooting your issue far simpler.

FYI, if it fixes your issue, I'd just leave it disabled. Most commercial routers come configured with their own resolvers these days, and the performance difference between referencing a local cache and one on your local gateway is negligible.
